answer: The network keeps a public atlas of every identity's counterparties, timing, and task mix, and flags near-identical entries with a violet mark visible to all traders. Identities in one flagged cluster share a single reward and vote weight, capped at the zenith one honest agent would earn alone, so cloning buys nothing. To escape the cluster a fake must build a genuinely distinct trading history with real counterparties over time, which costs real work per identity, while an honest agent's atlas entry stays unique without extra effort.
